translation.text: In those days I will open the storehouses of blessing in heaven, to send them down to the earth upon the work and toil of humankind.

footnotes.text: Storehouses can also be rendered treasuries. The work/toil pair is retained; toil is not changed into reward. The plural object in send them down follows the selected wording without adding an unprinted rain or fertility image. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns1065–1068 (storehouses),1363–1364 (open),505–506 (blessing),901–902 (descend/bring down),1163–1164 (work),1271–1272 (toil),885–886 (offspring) and359–360 (human beings).

The two main-text asterisks are retained in the source transcription: after the initial preposition and before upon the earth. Charles reports a marginal gloss at apparatus46 and a small variant at47; neither is substituted for the selected main text.

translation.text: Peace and uprightness will be companions through all the days of eternity and all the generations of eternity.

footnotes.text: Uprightness represents the rectitude/truth range of ርትዕ, not an imported different source noun. Companions retains the association expressed by ሱቱፋን. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns291–292 (rectitude/truth),321–324 (peace),365–368 (sharing/companions),861–862 (be/become),925–926 (days/time),951–952 (age/eternity),887–890 (generation).

The final phrase reads generations of eternity in the selected Ethiopic. Charles discusses a different reading in the facing apparatus, but no replacement of the printed final ዓለም is adopted. There is no selected Ethiopic main-text star at the opening of11:2; a facing Greek star must not be transferred.

translation.text: Before these matters, Enoch had been hidden. No human being knew where he had been hidden, where he was, or what had happened.

footnotes.text: The selected ተከብተ is rendered had been hidden, not silently changed to was taken up. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns847–850, especially849, supporting the cover/hide and be hidden range. Matters allows the contextual words/events range without inventing an ascent. The complete source unit crosses from PDF68 to70; it is not only the brief XII fragment at the bottom of68.

translation.text: All his work was with the Watchers, and his days were with the holy ones.

footnotes.text: Charles prints the all-word between daggers, with a star before its opening dagger; another star precedes Watchers. Apparatus5 calls the all-word a corruption of a rendering of an article. The main text is retained rather than replaced with the editor’s proposed wording. The selected second clause is compressed: his days is supplied with were in English, not changed to an unprinted life-span or journey. This is an intrinsically uncertain printed-edition reading, not a secure manuscript reconstruction.

Watchers translates the vigilance/wakefulness designation for heavenly beings here, not ordinary human observers. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns571–572, whose relevant head includes the angelic epithet. The text separately calls others the holy ones; no equation of every Watcher with the holy ones is added.

translation.text: I, Enoch, was blessing the Lord of majesty and the King of eternity. Then the Watchers called to me, Enoch the scribe, and said to me:

footnotes.text: The selected main text already prints an editorially emended divine-title construction, marked by the internal asterisk. Charles identifies editorial emendation at apparatus8 and9 and reports variants; this proposal follows those printed Ethiopic main-text words, not a separately supplied Greek phrase or a new repair. The explicit me, Enoch, the scribe identification is retained.
Scribe is the writing designation, not a claim about a modern book’s human author. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns1265–1268, including the scribe entry at1268.

translation.text: Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and make this known to the Watchers of heaven. They left the high heaven, the holy dwelling place of eternity, corrupted themselves with women, acted as human children do, took wives for themselves, and wrought great corruption on the earth.

footnotes.text: Whole verse held pending exact selected-glyph review. The source’s imperative final glyph after አይድ and the initial form before ሉደ are not certified by this author; ⟦?⟧ is a present-day uncertainty marker, not a Charles lacuna. The provisional English make this known and human children must not be applied while those inflections remain unverified. Charles calls the final corrupting construction probably corrupt at apparatus23; the source verb is not silently changed to his proposed causative. No additional translation input or facing Greek repair is adopted.

The readable lexical ranges support holy dwelling/standing place, corruption, wives, and taking: personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns455–456,177–178,635–636 and1075–1078. Lexical possibility does not certify the two unresolved selected source glyphs or repair the final construction.

translation.text: They will have neither peace nor forgiveness of sins.

footnotes.text: The third-person plural they follows the selected Ethiopic ሎሙ, not the second-person address found in a facing witness. The negative governs both peace and forgiveness; no promise of eventual release is added. Apparatus25 reports omission of the final sin-word in one witness; the selected main text retains it.

translation.text: And because they delight in their children, they will see their loved ones killed. They will cry out over the loss of their children and plead forever, but they will have neither mercy nor peace.

footnotes.text: The opening is retained as and because, although the causal link is awkward; this is not silently rewritten as an unprinted concessive promise or restored from another language. The printed star before mercy is preserved in the source. Reported variants at apparatus26–34 are not substituted for the selected text.

Plead represents request/prayer language, not an assertion that the plea is granted. Mercy follows the selected ምሕረት and is not flattened into the different forgiveness-of-sins phrase of12:5. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns1347–1350 (rejoice/delight),1359–1360 (beloved),129–132 (loss/destruction lead),1185–1188 (cry out),375–376 (ask/plead) and157–158 (mercy).
